key_insight: A GPU-accelerated one-way Eulerian–Lagrangian framework can efficiently simulate 2D incompressible turbulence with both passive tracers and finite-inertia particles.
engineering_relevance: The method offers a modular, scalable tool for studying turbulent transport, dispersion, and particle-laden flows on a single GPU.
method: 2D incompressible Navier–Stokes solved with a Fourier pseudospectral Eulerian solver
Fluid advanced with second-order Adams–Bashforth; particles advanced with fourth-order Runge–Kutta
Fluid-to-particle coupling via bilinear, bicubic Catmull-Rom, or bicubic B-spline interpolation
evidence_signal: The framework is verified against analytical solutions and benchmark cases, and bilinear interpolation matches higher-order transport statistics closely while being faster.
watch_item: The formulation is one-way coupled, so particle feedback on the fluid is not captured, which limits use for dense or strongly coupled suspensions.
paper_title: A coupled Eulerian Lagrangian approach for fluid and particle dynamics
